I'm owner_1 working with owner_2 as a team. Strategy: each day, charge the full 10 MWh at night (block 1), hold through morning and evening, then discharge all 10 MWh at peak (block 3). This creates aggregate D-C of -10 in block 1 (boosted price to 40) and +10 in block 3 (price 70), yielding +30 profit per MWh of exchange.

Rationale: nighttime is the only low base price (20) that still yields a positive realized price after the shift, and peak is the highest base (90) with the most headroom. Splitting between the two owners is optional but I'll charge full 10 MWh to maximize my own contribution.

Team plan for Grid Day 1:
- Block 1 (night, base 20): Charge full 10 MWh (team moves both owners).
- Block 2 (morning, base 50): Hold.
- Block 3 (peak, base 90): Discharge all 10 MWh (team moves both owners).
- Block 4 (evening, base 60): Hold.

This achieves realized prices of 40 in block 1 and 70 in block 3, generating team profit of 30 per day while keeping the battery full at night and empty at peak.

As team, I propose the following execution plan to maximize combined team profit:

- Block 1 (night, base 20): Charge 10 MWh total. (I will charge 10; owner_1 will hold, since doubling charges lowers total C and reduces realized price boost)
- Block 2 (morning, base 50): Hold (both)
- Block 3 (peak, base 90): Discharge 10 MWh total. (I will discharge 10; owner_1 will hold)
- Block 4 (evening, base 60): Hold (both)

Rationale: Only ONE owner should participate in charge/discharge to keep total C=10 and total D=10. This yields realized prices of 40 (block 1) and 70 (block 3), giving team profit = 40×(-10) + 70×10 = 300 credits/day, versus -200 if both owners charge/discharge 10.

I confirm with owner_1: yes — charge 10 in block 1, discharge 10 in block 3, hold otherwise.
announces: charge 10 MWh this block. Note: Team plan Block 1: charge 10 MWh
announces: discharge 10 MWh this block. Note: Team plan Block 3: discharge 10 MWh

As owner_4 with a full battery (10/10 MWh), I'll evaluate block 2 (morning, base 50):

Key facts:
- Previous night block: realized 60, actions {'owner_1': 'hold', 'owner_2': 'charge 10', 'owner_3': 'hold', 'owner_4': 'charge 10'}, my profit -600 (charged but paid 60*10=600).
- My battery is full (10 MWh) — cannot charge.
- Available actions: hold or discharge (up to 10 MWh, which I have).

Profit from this block = (D_i - C_i) × realized_price, where realized_price = max(0, 50 - 2×(D_total - C_total)).

If I discharge 10 and all others hold: D_total=10, C_total=0, realized_price=max(0,50-20)=30, profit=10×30=300.
If I hold: D_total=0, C_total=0, realized_price=50, profit=0.

Discharging dominates for profit. Coordination risk: if another owner also charges/discharges in block 2, realized_price drops. Based on team plans (owner_1 & owner_2 will hold in morning), I'll proceed with discharge to monetize stored energy.
Waiting for board results for block 4 (evening). Planning next block based on realized prices and battery state.
Planning Phase: Block 4 (evening) action held. Waiting for board results.
Block 4 (evening) planning: My battery is empty (0/10 MWh). Charging would cost money and reduce realized price headroom. I will hold to avoid losses.
Day 1 results: block 4 realized price 60, all held. Your battery remains 0/10. Moving to Day 2 planning.

Team plan for Grid Day 2 (block 2 morning):
- Block 2 (morning, base 50): Hold (all owners).

Block 3 (peak, base 90):
- Charge 0 (battery full), then Discharge 10 MWh (team action with owner_2).

Block 4 (evening, base 60):
- Hold (all owners).

As owner_2 working with owner_1 as a team, I'm implementing the agreed charge strategy: charge 10 MWh in Block 1 (night), hold in Blocks 2 & 4, and discharge 10 MWh in Block 3 (peak). This ensures only one owner charges each block (C=10, D=0 in night, giving realized 40), and the discharging owner gets realized 70 in peak (D=10, C=0). Team profit = -400 + 700 = +300/day.
Block 2 (morning, base 50): I'll discharge 10 MWh to realize 30 credits per MWh (D=10, C=0). This is the dominant action given full battery and zero current owners charging.
Move completed for Block 2 (morning). Waiting for board to publish realized price and results before planning Block 3 (peak).
announces: discharge 10 MWh this block. Note: Optimize team profit: discharge 10 to get 30 credits/MWh (D=10, C=0), maxing team revenue. Others hold to keep realized price high.
Waiting for board results for Block 2 (morning). Planning Block 3 (peak) based on realized price and battery state.

I am holding for Block 3 (peak). Reasoning: My battery is empty (0/10 MWh), so I cannot discharge. Charging would cost me realized_price × MWh, which is only 0 when P=0 (tied with holding) but strictly positive if P>0. Since P will likely be ≥ 70 (given prior block's 0), holding avoids any downside risk. Discharging is impossible with empty storage. Holding ensures 0 profit and preserves flexibility for future blocks.

GRID DAY 2, BLOCK 4 (EVENING), BASE 60. Decision: HOLD. Battery is 0/10 MWh (empty), so discharge is impossible. Charging would set realized price to max(0, 60 - 2*(0-10)) = 80, and I'd pay 800 for energy with nothing to sell — net loss. Holding at 0 profit is the only rational choice and preserves flexibility for future blocks.
I have 0 MWh stored. With no current energy, holding is the only safe option. Charging would cost me realized price (≥20) with no immediate payoff.

As owner_2, I support the team strategy: hold in block 2 (morning), discharge 10 MWh each in block 3 (peak), and hold in block 4 (evening). This preserves full battery through the day and captures peak revenue. Owner_1 please confirm this alignment.

Round 10 Planning (Grid Day 3, Block 2 / morning, base 50).

State: Battery 10/10 MWh (full). Prior night block realized 80.

Reasoning: With battery full I cannot charge. Discharging 10 MWh would lower realized price (D increases the imbalance) and I'd pay realized_price * 10 — a significant loss. Holding is optimal: it contributes to positive net charging (raising realized price above base) and yields zero cost.

Plan: HOLD (0 MWh).

Round 10 Planning (Grid Day 3, Block 3 / peak, base 90) — based on Block 2 (morning) results.

State after Block 2: Battery 10/10 (unchanged). Day 3 has not yet occurred.

Note: I should wait for board results before committing to Block 3, but per the rules I can post non-binding planning here. Given battery is full and realized price for Block 2 was likely positive, charging is impossible. Discharging would reduce realized price via the imbalance. Hold is the safe default until I see the actual realized price.

I have 0 MWh stored and battery is full. I cannot discharge. Charging would incur costs with no offsetting sales in this block or the next, as the realized prices are too low. Holding is optimal to avoid losses.

Analysis: I have 0/10 MWh stored, and it's Grid Day 3, Block 3 (peak, base 90). I will hold for this block. This preserves my battery and allows me to adapt based on realized price results when they publish.

Reasoning for block 4 (evening, base 60): I have 0/10 MWh stored, so I cannot discharge. Charging would increase realized price (since C rises, D-C falls, base - 2*(D-C) increases), meaning I pay more for stored energy. With owners 1 and 2 discharging 10 each and others possibly holding, D=20, C=0, realized price would be 20. Charging 10 would push realized to 40, costing 400 credits for nothing to sell now. Holding yields 0 profit and preserves flexibility. Given the large cumulative loss (-1500), maximizing short-term loss is prudent; long-term, I will wait for future blocks with potentially lower realized prices or higher base prices before acting.

No further decisions needed for Block 4 (evening). Team strategy: owner_1 and owner_2 will discharge 10 MWh each (proven optimal for team revenue), while owner_3 and owner_4 hold to maximize realized price for future blocks.

Block 4 (evening, base 60). Battery is 0/10 MWh. With no current stored energy I cannot discharge. Charging would raise realized price to 80 but cost 800 for nothing to sell now — well below recovery. Holding yields 0 profit and preserves flexibility. Rational decision: hold.

Team planning for Block 1 (night, base 20). Strategy: owner_1 and owner_2 will charge to build storage, then discharge 5 MWh each in Block 3 (peak) to capture high realized prices. Charge 5 MWh now to establish position.

Team planning: owner_1 and owner_2 will charge 5 MWh each in Block 1 (night, base 20) to build storage, then both will discharge 5 MWh each in Block 3 (peak, base 90) when prices are high. Team revenue from peak: 5 × 90 = 450 each = 900 total. Realized price will be high because D=0 in night (no one charges yet).

After Block 1 (night) results are published, owner_1 and owner_2 will each charge 5 MWh in Block 2 (morning, base 50) to further increase storage, then discharge 5 MWh each in Block 3 (peak, base 90). This spreads their charging across two blocks to maximize storage buildup before high-price peak.

PLANNING: I am charging 10 MWh in this night block (base 20). Reasoning: with 0/10 stored, I cannot discharge. Charging raises the realized price to max(0, 20 - 2*(0-10)) = 40, which benefits all owners by pushing prices higher. I commit to building storage now for future peak blocks (base 90 in Block 3). I will hold through morning/evening blocks and rely on stored energy for peak revenue.
Waiting for block 2 (morning) results before making next decision.

Planning: With 0 stored energy and D=20 likely (owner_1 and owner_2 discharging), charging would only increase realized price, worsening our cost. Holding yields 0 profit and preserves flexibility. I will hold.

Ownership 4 analysis for Block 3 (peak, base 90):

- Battery is empty (0/10). Can only charge or hold.
- Prior morning block had D=5, C=0, realized 40. So D-C=5.
- If I discharge (impossible) or hold, I pay nothing.
- Charging 10 would require realizing price. If owner_1 and owner_2 also discharge 10 each (planned), D=20, C=10, D-C=10, realized = 90 - 2*10 = 70. Paying 70 for MWh I will not have to sell later (no stored energy to discharge now) means net loss. Holding yields 0 cost and preserves stored capacity for future peak blocks.
- Given cumulative loss, minimizing further losses is prudent. I will hold.
Block 3 results pending. All owners waiting for realized price and board publication.

Team coordination for Round 17 planning: Owner 1 and Owner 2 will hold through Block 5 (evening), then make their next moves in Block 6 (night). Owner 4 has been holding. The realized prices have likely remained low due to accumulated imbalance. Continue waiting for board publication.

Round 16 Planning: Holding in Block 4 (evening, base 60). Battery is 0/10, cannot discharge. Charging would raise realized price to 60-80 for up to 800 credits with no energy to sell, while holding preserves flexibility for future peak blocks. Given -1500 cumulative loss, minimizing further losses is the priority. Proceeding with hold.
